name: Increase deliberation size
description: Increase the number of participants that can participate.
pros: Increase the number of people, variety of ideas, and diversity of people.
cons: Decrease depth of discussions and minimize marginalized voices.

name: Break into small facilitated groups
description: Divide the large group into smaller facilitated groups that deliberate in parallel and report back to plenary.
pros: Preserves depth of discussion at scale and keeps every voice heard.
cons: Requires many trained facilitators and coordination overhead.

name: Deepen the deliberation
description: Add more time, expert input, and structured discussion so participants can reason carefully.
pros: Produces more considered, higher-quality recommendations.
cons: Slower, more demanding for participants, and reaches fewer people.

name: Build a balanced information campaign
description: Provide clear, objective materials so the public understands the issue before engaging.
pros: Raises public understanding and sets a shared factual baseline.
cons: One-way communication gives participants little influence over outcomes.

name: Run structured feedback rounds
description: Gather public input through surveys, comment periods, and targeted consultations.
pros: Efficient way to collect broad input and surface concerns early.
cons: Feedback may not shape final decisions, risking consultation fatigue.

name: Establish ongoing working groups
description: Work directly with participants over multiple sessions so their concerns are consistently considered.
pros: Builds trust and ensures public aspirations are understood throughout.
cons: Time-intensive and demands sustained commitment from participants and staff.

name: Co-design with a stakeholder panel
description: Partner with participants to jointly develop alternatives and a preferred solution.
pros: Shared ownership improves legitimacy and the quality of proposals.
cons: Consensus-building is slow and can be dominated by organized interests.

name: Delegate decision authority
description: Place final decision-making power directly in the hands of participants.
pros: Maximizes legitimacy and public buy-in for the outcome.
cons: High political risk and requires institutional commitment to honor the result.

name: Adopt an online deliberation platform
description: Use a digital platform to host discussion, voting, and proposal-building remotely.
pros: Low cost, wide reach, and flexible participation across locations and schedules.
cons: Excludes those with poor digital access and can reduce discussion depth.

name: Host in-person deliberation events
description: Bring participants together physically for facilitated discussion.
pros: Richer dialogue, stronger relationships, and higher-quality deliberation.
cons: Higher cost and logistics limit reach and exclude those who cannot travel.

name: Combine in-person and online participation
description: Blend physical events with digital channels so people can join whichever way suits them.
pros: Balances reach with depth and widens who can take part.
cons: More complex to run and requires equitable integration of both channels.

name: Launch an open call for participants
description: Invite anyone interested to take part through a low-barrier open sign-up.
pros: Broad reach, low cost, and strong sense of openness.
cons: Self-selection skews toward the already-engaged and less representative groups.

name: Add representativeness safeguards
description: Layer targeted outreach and quotas on top of open recruitment to correct for skew.
pros: Keeps the process open while improving demographic balance.
cons: Adds recruitment effort and cannot fully match random selection.

name: Recruit by civic lottery
description: Select participants through stratified random sampling to mirror the wider population.
pros: Produces a demographically representative mini-public with high legitimacy.
cons: Costly to recruit and incentivize, and reaches only a small number of people.

name: Convene a Citizens' Assembly
description: Assemble a large, randomly selected body empowered to deliberate and issue binding recommendations.
pros: Gold-standard for legitimacy, representativeness, and considered judgment.
cons: Expensive, lengthy, and demanding to organize and sustain.

name: Run a Citizens' Jury
description: Convene a small randomly selected panel that hears evidence and deliberates to a verdict.
pros: Deep, high-quality deliberation with a representative small group.
cons: Very small sample limits reach and statistical representativeness.

name: Hold a Deliberative Poll
description: Survey a representative sample before and after informed deliberation to measure considered opinion.
pros: Reveals how informed opinion shifts and carries scientific credibility.
cons: Resource-heavy and requires expert facilitation and survey design.

name: Run a large-scale online consultation
description: Crowdsource ideas and feedback from a broad self-selected public through a digital platform.
pros: Reaches large numbers cheaply and surfaces a wide range of ideas.
cons: Prone to skew, low deliberative depth, and gaming without safeguards.

name: Facilitate deliberative workshops
description: Run structured in-person workshops where a small group works through the issue together.
pros: Intimate setting fosters trust and detailed, careful discussion.
cons: Limited scale and dependent on skilled facilitation.

name: Scale a representative mini-public
description: Combine random selection with hybrid delivery to run a large yet representative deliberation.
pros: Marries representativeness with reach across formats.
cons: Complex logistics and higher cost to coordinate both channels.

name: Mount a digital public information drive
description: Distribute balanced explainer content at scale through online channels.
pros: Cost-effectively informs a very large audience.
cons: Purely informational with minimal two-way engagement.
